sources.entry: Featherbar - Featherweight menu bar system monitor showing CPU, RAM, power, and temperature in two color-coded lines.

summary.one_liner: Featherbar is a tiny Rust macOS menu-bar app that shows live CPU, RAM, battery power, and CPU temperature on two color-coded lines, refreshed every 2 seconds.
summary.what_it_does: Featherbar places a two-line text readout in the macOS menu bar. The top line shows CPU percent and battery watts; the bottom line shows RAM percent and CPU temperature. Each value is colored green, orange, or red based on its own thresholds (CPU 40/70%, RAM 60/80%, power 10/20W, temperature 60/80°C), while labels stay neutral. Values use fixed-width fields in SF Mono so the layout does not shift as numbers change. The app runs on a single main-thread event loop that wakes on a 2-second timer, samples metrics, redraws, and sleeps. A right-click menu offers a Launch at login check item (via SMAppService, only when run as an .app bundle) and Quit. The README says adding a new metric requires an enum variant, a match arm, and a line-placement constant in src/main.rs.
use_cases: monitor CPU and RAM from the menu bar
see battery discharge watts at a glance
check CPU temperature without opening a dashboard
run a minimal system monitor with low memory use
auto-start a menu bar monitor at login
extend a Rust menu bar app with a new metric
notable: Zero background threads: a single main-thread tao event loop with WaitUntil timer wakes, and sysinfo's rayon pool is compiled out
Memory measured at about 11 MB at launch, settling near 20 MB steady state, with a profiled soak showing no featherbar leaks
Renders both lines into an NSImage so two rows fit in the status item, which a single-line title cannot do
Release binary around 800 KB via opt-level z, LTO, and strip
Explicitly out of scope: fans and total SoC power, to avoid undocumented IOKit/SMC keys
caveats: Requires macOS on Apple Silicon (M-series) and Rust 1.89+
Power figure is battery charge/discharge rate, so it reads 0W on AC or at full charge and is not total system power
Launch-at-login toggle only works from the .app bundle; a bare cargo run binary shows it disabled
Fans and total package power are not supported; the roadmap mentions a possible SMC-based reader
